resolutions.researcher_notes: Two distinct publishers agree the pipeline is a completed, operating asset. EIA's 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' database (government) lists 'Red Bluff Express Pipeline' with Status='Completed', Completed Date=2018-05-01, Year In Service Date=2018 -- 'Completed'/in-service is the prose-equivalent of the sheet's 'operating'. Independently, Western Midstream Partners LP's own FY2019 Q1 10-Q (SEC EDGAR, filed 2019-05-01) describes its January 2019 acquisition of a 30% interest in 'Red Bluff Express Pipeline, LLC,' reports actual 'equity investment throughput' increases attributable to Red Bluff Express, and lists ongoing equity income/distributions from it in its financial-statement tables -- i.e. a live, throughput-generating asset, not a project under construction. Two distinct origins (EIA/government database; Western Midstream's own SEC filing), independent: true, tier high.

Western Midstream's 10-Q states explicitly: 'Red Bluff Express ... owns a natural gas pipeline operated by a third party connecting processing plants in Reeves and Loving Counties, Texas to the WAHA hub in Pecos County, Texas.' EIA's database entry for this same pipeline sits in EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects register (the source file itself, EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx, is EIA's natural-gas-pipeline project tracking table) alongside a Project Notes field describing residue-gas takeaway ('Connects Orla and Waha plants for residue takeaway' -- 'residue' gas is processed natural gas). Two distinct origins agree this is a gas pipeline; tier high, independent: true.

EIA's database row for 'Red Bluff Express Pipeline' (Energy Transfer Co, TX RRC authority) states 'Completed Date' = 2018-05-01 and 'Year In Service Date' = 2018 -- an exact match to the sheet's StartYear1=2018. Single explicit source, medium tier, independent: false. Circumstantially corroborated (not cited as a standalone date match) by Western Midstream's Q1 2019 10-Q, which describes acquiring its 30% interest in an already-operating, throughput-generating pipeline in January 2019 -- consistent with, but not independently dating, a 2018 in-service date. Note: EIA's database separately lists a distinct 'Red Bluff Express Extension' project (25 additional miles, Year In Service Date=2019) -- an expansion of this same pipeline, not the original in-service event, and not used to support this unit's 2018 value.

EIA's database row states 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)' = 1400 for the original Red Bluff Express Pipeline project -- an exact match to the sheet's Capacity 1400.00 MMcf/d. Single source, medium tier, independent: false. Neither the Western Midstream 10-Q, the Energy Transfer earnings release, nor the MasTec/Pumpco construction page states a throughput-capacity figure, so no second corroborating source was found for this specific value.

EIA's database row states 'Miles' = 80 for the Red Bluff Express Pipeline -- an exact match to the sheet's LengthKnown 80.00 mi. Independently, MasTec's own project page (via its contractor Pumpco; the live mastec.com/projects/red-bluff page is currently 200 but was verified through this Wayback capture since the seed citation's original access date predates it) states: 'Pumpco constructed 65 miles of 42" diameter pipeline in Texas, as well as 10.4 miles of 36" diameter pipeline and 6.2 miles of 30" diameter pipeline from Coyanosa, Texas to Orla, Texas' and separately summarizes the job as '82 miles of large diameter pipeline in Texas' (65+10.4+6.2=81.6, rounded to 82) -- within ~2 miles of the sheet's 80, a reasonable variance between a construction contractor's total linear footage (which can include tie-ins/laterals) and the pipeline's official mainline length as logged by EIA. Two distinct origins (EIA government database; MasTec/Pumpco, the constructor) agree on ~80 miles; tier high, independent: true.

EIA's database row states 'Pipeline Diameter (Inches)' = '30,36,42' -- an exact match to the sheet's Diameter '30, 36, 42' in. MasTec/Pumpco's project page independently confirms the same three diameters by segment: 65 miles of 42-inch pipe, 10.4 miles of 36-inch pipe, and 6.2 miles of 30-inch pipe. Two distinct origins agree exactly; tier high, independent: true.

EIA's database Project Notes read: 'Connects Orla and Waha plants for residue takeaway' -- naming Orla, Texas, matching the sheet's StartPrefecture/District='Orla'. MasTec/Pumpco's project page independently states the line runs 'from Coyanosa, Texas to Orla, Texas,' again naming Orla and confirming Texas, United States for both ends (the sheet leaves EndLocation blank and only asserts State/Country=Texas/United States, which both sources support). Two distinct origins agree; tier high, independent: true. Western Midstream's 10-Q additionally situates the pipeline as 'connecting processing plants in Reeves and Loving Counties, Texas to the WAHA hub in Pecos County, Texas' -- consistent with Orla (Reeves County) as the start point.

The live BusinessWire URL for Energy Transfer's Q2 2023 results release could not be fetched directly (HTTP 403 on a direct curl retry with a browser User-Agent; not a confirmed 404/410, so per the hard rules this is a block, not a deletion) -- its Wayback capture was used instead and confirmed to carry the same content. That release's non-wholly-owned-subsidiaries ownership table states verbatim: 'Red Bluff Express 70.0 %' under Energy Transfer's percentage-ownership column -- an exact match to the sheet's Owner1=Energy Transfer / Owner1%=70.00%. Independently, Western Midstream Partners LP's own Q1 2019 10-Q (SEC EDGAR) states: 'In January 2019, we acquired a 30% interest in Red Bluff Express, which owns a natural gas pipeline operated by a third party' and 'We acquired our 30% interest from a third party via an initial net investment of $92.5 million' -- an exact match to Owner2=Western Midstream / Owner2%=30.00%, and the two figures (70%+30%) sum to 100%, consistent with the pipeline having exactly two owners. Two distinct publishers (Energy Transfer and Western Midstream), each independently reporting its own stake, agree exactly; tier high, independent: true. Neither the seed Western Midstream Q3 2022 earnings PDF (live URL 404s; Wayback capture at 20230314142953 exists but was not needed once the 10-Q gave a stronger primary-source ownership statement) nor the MasTec/Pumpco page (a construction contractor page, not an ownership source) was needed for this unit.
